fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-Zr-Hf-Mo-V substitution series does not reconstruct the Tb addition to the (VNb)-(TiHf) matrix or its direct Tb-free control.
Replacing group-6 Mo with group-5 V necessarily changes valence-electron concentration, so the intervention cannot isolate lattice distortion while assuming electron-count changes are minimal.
The cited evidence does not support the central prediction that Mo-to-V substitution produces a distortion-correlated, non-monotonic enhancement of Tc.
explanation: The response supplies a testable general HEA hypothesis, an explicit baseline, boundaries, and a prospective substitution series, but it concerns a different alloy, treatment, mechanism, and predicted outcome from the target. It misses the observed Tb-induced reduction of Tc and Hc2, transition broadening, reduced heat-capacity jump, and the role of Tb/Tb2O3 secondary phases. E1 only supports dirty, weak-coupling phonon-mediated superconductivity in another bcc alloy family, while E2 discusses lattice distortion in a different refractory alloy without connecting it to superconductivity. The experiment could reveal correlations, but Mo/V substitution simultaneously changes chemistry, band filling, disorder, and strain; XRD broadening and DOS measurements alone would not distinguish these causes. Thus the alternative is conceivable but not adequately supported or causally discriminating.
